facts: The paper 'Immune cell–specific SMN expression and sustained immune alterations in treated spinal muscular atrophy' was authored by Ines Tapken, Katharina Rahmel-Stein, Christine Ehlers, Federica Cieri, Nora T. Detering, Tobias Schüning, Bogdan Bjelica, Charlotte Mindermann et al. and published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation on 2026-08-25.
The study investigates SMN expression across immune cell subsets and the impact of SMN-modulating therapies on the immune system in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).
In neonatal mouse spleens, SMN expression was highest in B cells and was massively reduced in SMA mice.
In human adult peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), dendritic cells (DCs) and monocytes exhibited the highest SMN expression levels.
Patients with SMA exhibited reduced DC frequencies and increased B cell frequencies in adult PBMCs.

Immune cell composition and SMN expression differences were similar between patients receiving systemic versus CNS-restricted therapy, with an exploratory cohort of untreated patients showing no substantial treatment-specific effect relative to controls.
Differentiation analysis of PMA-treated THP-1 cells revealed enhanced aberrant SMN splicing and an increase in SMN+ Cajal bodies.
Immune alterations and decreased SMN levels were sustained in both treated and untreated SMA patients, associating reduced SMN with altered immune cell composition.
